name: Feline leukaemia virus (FeLV)
short_description: An enveloped gammaretrovirus (~80-100 nm) that infects the blood-forming cells of the bone marrow and spreads through mutual grooming, shared bowls and saliva. Unlike its sibling FIV (a lentivirus with a CONE-shaped core), FeLV is a classic 'C-type' particle: barely-visible short Env spikes over the envelope, and a roughly SPHERICAL, centrally-placed condensed core (capsid p27) that assembles at the plasma membrane at the same moment it buds off.

textbook.1: ❌ FAIL — capsid clearly spherical and centred (correct, not conical), muted educational palette matching house style, but a magnified crop of the two 'coiled RNA' strands showed one strand had a sharp angular zigzag kink partway down — a shape close enough to a digit/letter glyph to trip the skill's known 'coiled RNA forms legible characters' failure mode (the FIV sibling hit this exact issue). Re-prompted with an explicit 'smooth flowing curves only, no sharp angles or kinks, must not form any letter/digit/symbol' instruction.
textbook.2: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — RNA now two clean smooth wavy lines with no kinks or letter-like shapes (re-checked by magnified crop); capsid is a true circle, concentric with the cream matrix ring and teal envelope, centred in the frame — verified round/centred (not conical) both by direct view and by radial pixel scan from the image centre outward (amber capsid 0–240px, cream matrix ring 245–275px, teal envelope 280–385px, all concentric); short sparse oval Env knobs on the envelope; no baked-in text elsewhere, no border (edge pixels sampled ≈RGB(80,85,85), matching the interior charcoal, no black band).

sem.1: ❌ FAIL — technically round and budding-from-membrane as composed, but the framing filled the whole canvas with an oversized membrane swell and two large domed particles that read as skin blisters/pimples rather than an isolated virus plate, and did not match this atlas's own SEM house style (compare the accepted FIV SEM render: one small centred sphere resting on a substrate with generous margin). Re-prompted to drop the budding-membrane composition and return to a single centred sphere with generous margin, per house style.
sem.2: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — single centred sphere, generous margin on all sides, resting on a faintly textured substrate with soft shadow, false-colour rose-coral palette; surface has only a sparse scatter of very low, shallow domes (barely-visible Env knobs per ICTV's description of Gammaretrovirus spikes), correctly reading as SPHERICAL and CENTRED (checked by direct view — the specimen's own silhouette is a true circle, unlike a conical/teardrop shape); no cutaway (correct for SEM — surface only); no baked-in text; edge pixels sampled dark charcoal gradient, no black border.

3d.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — accepted on the first attempt. Clear concentric-sphere construction: translucent teal envelope, pale tan matrix layer, and a distinct ROUND amber-gold capsid sitting dead-centre and equidistant from the envelope in every direction — confirmed spherical/centred by direct view AND by pixel colour sampling along the horizontal/vertical axes from the image centre (amber 0–110px, tan matrix 120–185px, teal envelope 190–290px, symmetric on both +x and -y scans, i.e. genuinely concentric, not off-centre like a cone would read). Sparse short coral Env knobs sit nearly flush against the envelope, never tall/stalked. Two magenta RNA springs checked by magnified crop — clean coiled-spring shapes, no letter-like crossings. No baked-in text, no border, natural (not neon, not monochrome) biological tints.

watercolor.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — accepted on the first attempt. Warm aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge with a soft darker wash halo directly on the paper (no separate mat/frame/sheet-on-surface look, matching the cocci/rod-bacterium house style — confirmed by corner pixel sampling, all four corners read as paper tan ≈RGB(240,220,185)). The core reads as a clean circle, centred, holding two smooth rose-magenta RNA wavy lines (checked by magnified crop — no sharp kinks, no letter shapes) and small teal enzyme flecks; a pale gray lens/ring motif represents the matrix layer around the core; short blunt knob bumps ring the outer teal-green envelope, sparse and irregular, never spiky. No baked-in text, no border.

reference: A freely-licensed FeLV micrograph WAS found and used: CDC Public Health Image Library image #5610, "Transmission electron micrograph showing ultrastructural morphology of feline leukemia virus (FeLV) particles" — public domain (U.S. federal government work; PHIL's usage-terms field reads 'None — This image is in the public domain and thus free of any copyright restrictions'). Mirrored on Wikimedia Commons at File:Feline_leukemia_virus.JPG, confirmed via the Commons imageinfo API to be the native, full-resolution file at 1808×1200 px (432,753 bytes) — no higher-resolution master exists, so no upscale was applied; fetch_reference.py downloaded this exact URL and centre-cropped/resized to 1080×1080 for the atlas. KNOWN COMPROMISE: this is a dense, busy negative-stain plate showing numerous overlapping membrane fragments and particles rather than a single isolated virion — per the verification rubric a group image is acceptable only if the microbe's features remain readable, and several individual round, electron-dense particles ARE clearly resolvable in the frame (including a couple of cup/bud-like profiles consistent with C-type particles budding from membrane), which is why it was accepted rather than rejected as a dense clump. It has no baked-in text or scale bar (confirmed against the original Commons master before cropping), so edit_image.py was not run — nothing needed cleaning, and running it risked re-illustrating a plate whose grainy authenticity is the point.
